recipes.name: Black Bean and Corn Salad
ingredients_raw: 2 (15 ounce) cans black beans, rinsed and drained

steps.text: Place olive oil, lime juice, garlic, salt, and cayenne pepper in a small jar. Close the lid tightly and shake the jar until the dressing is well combined.
Combine beans, thawed corn, avocado, bell pepper, tomatoes, green onions, and cilantro in a salad bowl.
Shake dressing again, pour over salad, and toss to coat.

raw_recipe.headline: Black Bean and Corn Salad
raw_recipe.description: This colorful black bean and corn salad has a refreshing lime and garlic dressing and makes a great side dish for any occasion.

review.reviewBody: Great bean salad! I added much more lime juice, more garlic, a bit more salt and reduced the oil. Plus, I did equal amounts of corn and beans. Also, to avoid "mushiness", I added the tomato and avacado very last, after mixing the dressing in with the other ingredients. I gave it one last toss just before serving to coat the avacado and tomato. Very good!

This salad is so yummy and super versatile. It’s great by itself, or for a full dinner we like to grill some chicken breasts and throw it all on baked corn tortillas with lettuce for a tostada salad. The only changes to the actual salad we make are that we use finely diced purple onion instead of the green onion and add a bit more spice to the dressing. I’m not a cilantro fan by any means, but I think it’s vital to this salad. I just chop it very fine and use a little less. The only problem I have with this salad is that it doesn’t make the best leftovers. It’s tasty the next day, but the tang of the lime and the cilantro can’t survive the cold of the ‘fridge overnight and it loses it’s ‘zing.’ Definitely the best on the day it's made.
The avocado will turn brown if the salad is not eaten right away. I suggest making the salad without the avocado ahead of time and adding it before serving.

I read the comments before trying this salad. I used 2 TBSP of extra virgin olive oil, no more. I added half cup of freshly squeezed lime juice. Two 19 oz cans of black beans and two cups of frozen peach and cream corn kernels. This salad was out of this world. I might have had 3/4 cups pf cilantro instead of half a cup like the recipe ask for. I let it sit in the fridge for 6 to 8 hours before serving it. It is a fresh summery taste. It could be easily eaten as a lunch meal. Great recipe, thanks for the comments, that's what makes it better. I never tried this recipe with the original quantities, it might be great but I am not big on oily salad and we are all bananas over lime juice. Thanks to Jen for submitting this recipe and also thanks to everyone who submitted comments. Enjoy!

Fresh and fabulous! I grilled three ears of fresh corn for 10 mins until charred on all sides and cut it off the cob. It added a whole new level of flavor to the dish. I used a 1/2 tbsp of smoked sea salt and 1 tsp of cumin to the dressing. Also zested the lime into the dressing. We served this with lime tortillas as a salsa. Also good on chicken nachos, tacos, and fish tacos!

Followed directions exactly so I'll know what to tweak if I need to. Delicious and quite lovely in appearance. In the future, I will keep the avo and tomatoes separate until right before eating as the tomato gets watery and the avos go brown. Love the dressing. I will add more garlic to suit my obsession but exactly as instructed here, it was great! 5 Stars all the way

I made a smaller salad by using half of each of the ingredients. I ate two servings and describe it as flavorful, zesty and refreshing. Easy to make and a treat as no cooking required. It would be interesting to make it with lemons instead of limes.

I did read the reviews, I agreed with most the changes, and of course, it boils down to personal preference. I've made enough salads to know, a 1/2 cup is way too much oil, a quarter to third cup is fine. Also, someone mentioned, (and you can look it up), adding the avocado pit has nothing to do with keeping the avocado from turning brown. It's the Citric acid alone in the lime juice that keeps the avocado from turning brown. Look it up. For the tomato, I went ahead and just added it. The only difference, I did not include the center watery portion, with the seeds and all. That is what makes it more watery. I used Roma tomato's and patted them lightly with a paper towel. I'll be making this again. I made it ahead of time, the flavors relax and blend together, IMO.
So good...just added some raw zucchini chunks and charred 2 cobs of corn on the BBQ before cutting it off the cob.

This was so-o-o good. I followed the tips offered in two of the previous suggestions, that is, increased the ratio of lime juice to olive oil and added the tomatoes and avocado last -- for the final light toss -- to keep them from being crushed. For my own tastes, I skipped the cayenne pepper, garlic and added a chopped green pepper. The flavors were a terrific mixture of colors and textures. The cilantro, lime juice and onion were a perfect complement.

Pretty good! I gave it four because I saw the other reviews on the Olive oil being too much, so I did a test on a little, and they were right. Cut the oil down to 1/4 cup. I added a dash of cumin. Made it good for a healthy side dish. Thanks for this oh, and I used leftover black beans from fridge that I made earlier in the week from scratch. Worked perfectly with a half bag of frozen corn. Fantastic

Love this recipe and have made it several times. Absolutely fine as written. I've also had great results with these substitutions (based on what I had on hand): drained canned corn instead of frozen; halved cherry tomatoes instead of chopped; crumbled Cotija cheese instead of avocado, or in addition to it. Thanks for posting!
I loved the flavors and the homemade dressing made it so tasty 😋
I made this according to the recipe, and it was scrumptious. I’m taking it to a family gathering tomorrow because I’m sure it will be a hit.
Added a Jalapeno, paprika and a little chili powder. Awesome on it's own though too. Easy to adjust based on available veggies too. Added more red bell pepper also for the crunch factor.
My moms favorite
I don’t know why the recipe calls for frozen corn, but it is way too frozen .. no instructions to thaw or anything. I would use canned corn
I made it with fresh (grilled) corn on the cob. Delicious!!!
I added a half of a cucumber chopped and a half a red onion instead of the green onions because that is what I had.
This is a fantastic and simple recipe. I used more corn than called for and added sautéed chicken to make it a main dish. Delicious!
